script.text: Russia and Ukraine are about to talk again, while missiles still hit Kyiv. Reuters sources say Yemen's Houthis are within fifty miles of Aden. And Iran says its missiles have no range limit.

Five stories, ranked by impact. Number one is the Iran war, where strikes, a draft deal and a strait Iran says stays closed all happen at once. And on November tenth, Russia and Ukraine are due to sit down in Abu Dhabi, for the first U.S.-mediated talks since February.

Number five is a vote in South Africa. Municipal elections were held this week, and early results show a sharp drop for the ruling African National Congress. The ANC had about thirty-two percent in early counts, according to the Associated Press. That is roughly fourteen points below its result in twenty twenty-one. The opposition Democratic Alliance was close behind, and led narrowly in some early counts in Johannesburg, the country's biggest city. Municipal councils run city services like water, electricity and waste collection, so these votes reach daily life. No party won an outright majority in the early results. These numbers are early and can still change. When no party wins a majority, councils are usually run through coalition deals. The ANC has governed nationally since the end of apartheid in nineteen ninety-four. Next: a rebel advance in Yemen.

Number four is the war in Yemen. On November second, Reuters reported that Houthi forces had advanced to within eighty kilometers, about fifty miles, of Aden, the temporary capital of the internationally recognized government. Aden sits on the Gulf of Aden, near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the route toward the Suez Canal. Four military sources told Reuters it is the closest the group has come to the city since the early months of the war in twenty fifteen. The Houthis also took the Maqatirah district, which overlooks the road between Taiz and Aden. Reuters' sources say the push could let the Houthis outflank government forces on the mountains overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. A Houthi camp is about fifty kilometers from Lahj province, and eighty from Aden, according to Reuters. Taiz, Yemen's third largest city, has been encircled since early October, Reuters reports. In September, AP reported, the Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mokha. In October, Al Jazeera reported, Yemen's leader announced an operation to retake Houthi-held land. On November fourth, government forces claimed control of the al-Jawf mountain range, Al Jazeera reported. Reuters also reported that the Houthis struck Aden airport after warning people to evacuate. AP describes the Houthis as Iran-backed. Next: the alliance Saudi Arabia is building.

Number three is a defense pact taking shape around Saudi Arabia. Quick question. Which country joins Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in the Mecca Defence Alliance? Take a guess. Turkey. The three signed the pact on August seventh, and Turkey's parliament has now ratified it, clearing the way for military support to Saudi Arabia. Turkish officials describe the pact as defensive. Meanwhile, the Saudi and Syrian defense ministries signed a military cooperation agreement during Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa's visit to Riyadh, according to Semafor. Its terms have not been made public. Syria's foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, said discussions are underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the alliance. An analyst told Middle East Eye that the talks are at an early stage, and that Syria is unlikely to join soon. Next: the talks returning to Abu Dhabi.

Number two is Ukraine. U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff announced that the United States will mediate Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on November tenth and eleventh, with Jared Kushner also on the American team. The Kremlin has confirmed the dates. Axios and other outlets report these would be the first U.S.-mediated talks since February, a gap of nine months. Kyiv Post describes them as working level. Witkoff listed security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues on the agenda. No concessions have been announced so far. Meanwhile, the strikes continue. On November second, Zelenskyy said Russian attacks hit power infrastructure in four regions and left hundreds of thousands without electricity. Ukraine says it shot down three hundred seventy-one of four hundred thirty-three drones. Russia says Ukrainian drones hit an industrial site in Nizhny Novgorod. This weekend, AP reported that missiles targeting Kyiv wounded five people, and Zelenskyy accused Russia of escalating strikes before the talks. Next: the Iran war.

Number one is the Iran war. On November second, three U.S. officials told CBS News that American forces carried out limited defensive strikes near the Strait of Hormuz. This week, President Trump confirmed new limited strikes on an Iranian air defense system, which he called minor. At the same time, Qatar has presented a draft memorandum of understanding. Reports citing sources close to the mediators say the United States approved it. Qatar says both sides are reviewing it, and a senior Iranian official told Reuters the two sides are far from a deal. Mohsen Rezaei, an Iranian security official, says Hormuz reopens only after Iran's seven conditions are met. On Thursday, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire, and that one tanker hit a mine. That claim is unverified. On Saturday, a Guard spokesman said Iran's limit of about two thousand kilometers on missile range has been lifted. The Associated Press notes Iran is not known to have longer-range missiles. In late October, Gulf states were reportedly told to prepare for a possible short, intense campaign, according to Middle East Eye and the Wall Street Journal as cited by Fox News. Axios reported before the midterms that Israel's prime minister was pressing Trump to strike after the vote, while Secretary of State Rubio said Trump had made no decision. The United States says its naval blockade of Iranian ports continues. About a fifth of the world's oil normally passes through Hormuz, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Here are the dates to watch. On November tenth and eleventh, Russian and Ukrainian delegations are due to meet in Abu Dhabi. On Iran, Qatar's draft memorandum remains under review in both capitals, and Iran says Hormuz stays closed until its conditions are met. In Yemen, the fight for the road between Taiz and Aden is the front to watch. And in South Africa, final municipal results will show whether the early numbers hold. Will the Abu Dhabi talks produce any agreement? Tell us in the comments: yes or no.
Next Wednesday: who the Houthis are, and how a rebel movement came to threaten one of the world's busiest sea routes.

upload.title: Hormuz, Yemen, Abu Dhabi: Top 5 Stories of the Week
upload.description:
Five stories shaped the week of November 2 to 8, 2026: South Africa's ruling ANC dropping in early municipal results, the Houthi advance to within 80 kilometers of Aden in Yemen, the Mecca Defence Alliance and Saudi Arabia's new defense agreement with Syria, the U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks planned for Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11, and the Iran war with new strikes, a Qatari draft memorandum and Iran's announcement that it has lifted its missile range limit. Every claim is attributed to the source that reported it; unverified claims are labelled as such.
